summary: BLM lookout in Lake County: first built 1963, replaced under a 2010 federal recovery contract by a 50-foot block tower completed in January 2011; staffed in summers.

facts.design: unique BLM design: a 50-foot block tower with an enclosed observation cab; replaced a 1963 tower with a 10-foot concrete base and wooden live-in cab

access.note: active staffed BLM lookout on public land; in a May 2022 visit the primitive campground at its base was locked behind a gate and closed for the season

visit.trail_note: campground at the base is a few hundred feet from the lookout; the road is rough but should be passable to most vehicles with caution (Roaming Civic, May 2022)

events.note: original BLM lookout: two-story house, 15 1/2 feet square, concrete block lower story and frame upper story; BLM bids called October 1963; Klamath Falls contractor; a 1964 newspaper says it was built the summer before, which does not fit the October bid date
a temporary lookout with Mrs. Hazel Ward as lookout was in place before the new building
Bill Friday was the primary lookout until an injury at the end of August; Wendy Parker held the post for the rest of the season

February 18, 2010 federal solicitation (ARRA-funded) to demolish the existing tower and outhouse and build a new road, residence and tower; firelookout.com and Roaming Civic date the new tower to 2010
new 50-foot enclosed cinder block tower and observation cab; NHLR gives 2011 as the construction year; the Oregon Lookouts history page says completed January 2011
National Historic Lookout Register registration date June 23, 2022

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and The Roaming Civic say the new tower was built in 2010, and NHLR says constructed in 2011. The Oregon Lookouts history page shows a February 2010 contract and a January 2011 completion. The story uses 2010 for the contract and work and January 2011 for completion.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 2011 build year is supported by NHLR and the Oregon Lookouts history page; firelookout.com and Roaming Civic say 2010 (contract and work year). Unresolved: a 1964 newspaper says the first house was built 'last summer', but BLM bids were not called until October 1963, so the 1963 build season is uncertain; the story says 1963 with the caveat. Brief's record lacks the 1963 predecessor and its 10-foot base; events added. height_m 15.2 is the 50-foot tower. Elevation sources: NHLR 5,188 ft, firelookout.com 5,190 ft; brief 1581.3 m kept. Staffing is undated (firelookout.com). Access is 'restricted' from a 2022 gated campground, not from any BLM access rule; no rental found. Sources 3 and 4 show the 1963 tower's wooden live-in cab; minor distance conflict (19 vs 20 miles) not used in story.
